title: Commentary on Ecclesiastes
english: It should be noted that here 'bosom' is used as a synonym for the soul; for no one would say that anger rests in the sensible bosom. Regarding Ecclesiastes 7:10, do not say: 'What happened that the days that were before were better than these?' because you did not inquire about this in wisdom. If 'the fear of the Lord adds days' (Eccl 7:1), it is for us to enjoy the good or better days of holy knowledge.

To think that things are given to the elders according to time and the first things of knowledge is not wise; for even if something is ancient, it is not necessarily worthy of honor, since even evil is ancient, but it is not worthy of being honored because of time, if 'not the long-lived are wise, nor do the elders understand judgment' (Eccl 7:15).

Regarding 'good wisdom with inheritance, and abundance to those who behold the sun' (Eccl 7:11), and 'for wisdom is like the shadow of silver, and an abundance of knowledge will vivify the one beside it' (Eccl 7:12): just as those who behold the sun possess something more than those who have beheld it but no longer behold it, so those who happen to have wisdom and have authority over it have possessed something more—this is what is meant by 'with inheritance'—than those who received it and fell from it through their own lawlessness. For everyone who has acquired wisdom and lost it first acquired a shadow of wisdom and not wisdom, and later it seems as if a man had acquired a shadow of silver but had not acquired silver; for wisdom is by nature not something merely received, but it vivifies the one who possesses it through knowledge.

Regarding 'there is a righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and there is a godless man living in his wickedness' (Eccl 7:15-16), destruction is called so, as is the abandonment through testing, as in the case of Job: 'I have perished, for he says, and I have become a stranger' (Job 3:23). 'But from me a little,' says the...

title: The Peril of Immoderate Piety and the Timing of Death
english: David says, 'My feet have slipped; a little while my steps were poured out,' because I sought peace among those who work iniquity, seeing sinners (Ps 69:2).

Do not become too righteous, and do not philosophize excessively, lest you be struck with amazement (Eccl 7:16). Do not be impiously excessive and do not become harsh, so that you do not die at an inopportune time (Eccl 7:17). It is good that you hold fast to this, and indeed do not withdraw your hand from this, for he who fears God will emerge from all things (Eccl 7:18). Do not let an impious thought be lodged in your heart, lest your soul, having been impious, die in ignorance. The Sodomites and the Gomorrites died at their inopportune time (Gen 19). And if this time is a time of uprightness, those dying in this time and being separated from the life that is to come—'I am the life' (John 14:6)—do not die at an inopportune time.

It is good that you hold fast to not being too righteous, and indeed do not withdraw your heart from impiety, for fearing God, he will emerge from every evil. Guard the mouth of a king (Prov 21:1). Now 'mouth' refers to the word or the commandment. For even I know that it will be good for those fearing God, so that they may fear from his face (Eccl 8:12); and it will not be good for the impious, and he who does not fear from the face of God will not prolong his days in the shadow (Eccl 8:13). Now 'good' refers to the knowledge, the knowledge of God. It is vanity which has been made upon the earth (Eccl 1:2), that if they are righteous, it comes to them as a work of the impious, and if they are impious, it comes to them as a work of the righteous; I said that even this is vanity. It is vanity, he says, which happens upon the earth, that they are righteous and as...

title: The Unjust and the Heart's Inquiry
english: The impious fall into misfortunes, and they are impious and yet enjoy good things as if they were righteous. For concerning these things the prophet says to the Lord: 'But I will speak judgments to you: why is the way of the impious prosperous?' (Ps 73:18) and David: 'A little while, he says, my steps were poured out; for I sought peace among the lawless, seeing the sinners' (Ps 37:10).

That with all this I gave into my heart, and my heart with all saw this. The man approaches things to the heart, turning them aside for their investigation, and after these things the heart knows the things; and this is the 'I encircled, and my heart to know.' For the thing circles, and the one approaching it to the heart through examination, and the heart again knowing it. But this must be known, that not all things which the man circles and the heart knows; for we examine many things, but we know few.
That there is no making and thought and knowledge and wisdom in Hades, where you go. If there is no thought in Hades, how does the rich man entreat Abraham to send Lazarus to him? (Luke 16:24)
And the man did not know his time. The man did not know that time is the season of uprightness; for time signifies the opportune moment.

And walk in the ways of your heart, blameless, and in the vision of your eyes, in practice and in contemplation (Ps 119:9). And turn away anger from your heart and lead away evil from your flesh. From here we know that the passionate part is joined to the heart, and the lustful part to the flesh. Now he says evil: the fornication and the gluttony.
